question: Who was Ibn Turka?
proposition: Ibn Turka was a Shiʿi esotericist, openly Shiʿi in confessional allegiance.
reasoning: MK reports the position as Corbin's 'brief but warm embrace' of Ibn Turka as a standard-issue Shiʿi esotericist (pdf p.23), in the chapter on the R. Shaqq-i Qamar, one of only two sustained Western treatments (p.36).
The evidence Corbin leans on is a work (the R. Shaqq-i Qamar), not the Tamhid and not the apologies; MK reports no other basis.

MK's objection: absent the context of his own study Corbin's assertion is 'perfectly reasonable', but it ignores the Sunni-Shiʿi confessional ambiguity of the age (p.86), and MK lists it, with the Tamhid focus, among the errors of the other characterizations (p.25).
MK notes that Jean Aubin made the same assumption in 1957 and later changed his mind (p.86 n.125).

MK is a partisan reporter: he argues a rival reading and calls this one an error. He also marks the death date in Corbin's chapter title with [sic] (p.36 n.60). Confidence records how fully the pages of MK's dissertation let us reconstruct this position and its grounds, not whether it is true.
